stage0Implications: Treat this fixture as variable frame timing. The nominal and average frame rates differ and 44 distinct video packet durations were observed, so ST-004 must map proxy frames through observed presentation timestamps instead of dividing a frame index by the nominal rate.
Both streams start before zero on their own time base, so the import path must preserve the container start offset rather than assuming the first presentation timestamp is zero.

Presentation reordering is normal for this HEVC stream. 31160 of 62316 video packets are reordered while no decode timestamp regression was observed, so reordering alone must not be reported as a corruption indicator.

Full software decode of the 6.49 GB source took about 11.4 minutes on the recorded machine. Stage 1 must not require a full decode for interactive editing and must rely on the proxy path measured in ST-004.

The 61 recorded stderr lines were emitted by the null muxer used for verification, and the run still exited zero under -xerror while the decoder reported no error lines. Whether the same messages appear for real render targets must be confirmed in ST-005 and ST-012 rather than assumed.

assessment.sourceIntegrity: The container reported a size matching the file on disk, the probe score reached the maximum value, and the full decode completed without a decoder error.
openQuestions: The relationship between the null-muxer timestamp collisions and the variable frame timing is not yet measured. ST-004 and ST-012 provide the evidence.
No constant-frame-rate proxy has been produced yet, so the reversibility of the time mapping is unverified until ST-004.
